subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should agent-owned scheduler jobs introduced by experimental Claws be deleted by the canonical `agents delete` lifecycle, or may they remain Claw-specific resources after a normal agent deletion?
rationale: The branch intentionally chooses a Claw-only teardown path, while the reviewer identified the resulting orphan-job behavior; resolving the permanent ownership boundary changes core deletion semantics and cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Adopt canonical agent deletion
options.body: Update the generic agent-deletion lifecycle to remove agent-owned cron jobs transactionally before its config commit, and keep Claw removal as a provenance-aware wrapper around it.

options.title: Keep Claw-only teardown
options.body: Accept that ordinary agent deletion can leave recurring Claw jobs and document a supported cleanup/recovery path, with explicit maintainer approval of that contract.

options.title: Split the feature boundary
options.body: Land only a read-only Claw cron representation later and defer all scheduler mutation until the canonical deletion contract is established.

recommendation.title: Adopt canonical agent deletion
recommendation.body: Update the generic agent-deletion lifecycle to remove agent-owned cron jobs transactionally before its config commit, and keep Claw removal as a provenance-aware wrapper around it.

likelyOwner.reason: Their review established the concrete canonical-deletion invariant and they are the clearest history signal for this lifecycle decision.
